hero.title: Thanthai Roever Institute of Agriculture and Rural Development
hero.summary: TRIARD is a St. John Sangam Trust agriculture college at Valikandapuram in Perambalur district. Its educational history begins with diploma study in 1994, followed by degree teaching. The college is affiliated to TNAU, and its audited ICAR agriculture entry runs through March 2031.

overview.heading: Agriculture and rural development at Valikandapuram
paragraphs: Thanthai Roever Institute of Agriculture and Rural Development belongs to the Roever educational group and is run by St. John Sangam Trust. Its history records agriculture diploma teaching from 1994 and horticulture diploma teaching from 2001, with degree education developed later.

At Valikandapuram, the college describes 51.97 hectares, or 128.4 acres, used for practical learning and a crop cafeteria. Students considering the agriculture degree can ask how crop observations and field assignments connect with laboratory teaching. TRIARD also publishes scholarship-cell support and named graduate destinations, which applicants can discuss alongside a current prospectus and a recent cohort report.

programmes.name: B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture
programmes.summary: The official admission page describes a four-year B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture. Its published subject combinations centre on Physics, Chemistry and biological sciences, but the page includes a 2025–26 form and older portal guidance.
programmes.eligibility: Historical official admission page: 10+2 with the listed science combinations, including Physics, Chemistry and Biology or Botany/Zoology. Current subject equivalence and minimum marks must be checked in the entry-year TNAU prospectus.
programmes.admission_route: The college states TNAU online application is mandatory for both counselling and management admission; the page contains older portal references.

fees.note: A dated official fee schedule with tuition, compulsory charges and residential costs was not verified.

programmes.icar_scope_note: The audited ICAR row covers B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at Thanthai Roever Institute of Agriculture and Rural Development for 2026-03-16 to 2031-03-15. Printed intake is retained in recognition as historical scope.

admissions.heading: Applying through TNAU counselling
admissions.intro: TRIARD’s published procedure directs both counselling and management applicants to TNAU registration. Because the page combines older instructions with a 2025–26 form, its stated application charges and links are not adopted as current.
eligibility_points: A recognised 10+2 science qualification is described in the historical college admission page.
Confirm the current TNAU subject combinations and category thresholds before applying.

campus.heading: A crop cafeteria and practical teaching land
campus.intro: TRIARD describes agricultural land used for practical teaching and a crop cafeteria. Its facilities page lists a college library, language laboratory, laboratories and residential arrangements, but includes older details that should be reconfirmed before making accommodation plans.

scholarships.heading: Scholarships and financial support
scholarships.text: TRIARD’s Scholarship Cell describes help with government applications, verification and renewals. The official page lists post-matric and community schemes, but does not establish an individual award amount or current eligibility for every agriculture student.

schemes.name: Post-matric and community scholarship application support
schemes.details: The cell lists post-matric, BC/MBC/DNC, SC/ST and other schemes. Eligibility and availability depend on the current funding authority rules; amounts were not verified.

placements.heading: Career support and outcomes
placements.text: TRIARD’s 2025–26 outcomes table names graduates and their roles in banks, public agencies and agricultural businesses. Examples include agricultural/rural-development roles at Indian Bank and Punjab National Bank and research work at CARDS, TNAU. It is a list of reported outcomes, not a cohort-wide placement percentage or salary report.

recruiters.name: 2025–26 graduate destinations reported by the college
recruiters.description: The named table includes Indian Bank, Punjab National Bank, Federal Bank, Cotton Corporation of India and Sathyam Kissan Care. These destinations are not represented as a guaranteed campus-recruiter list.

faqs.question: Is TRIARD an independent university?
faqs.answer: No. The audited entry identifies a private college affiliated to TNAU.

faqs.question: What does the 1994 establishment date refer to?
faqs.answer: The college’s history dates the start of agriculture diploma courses to 1994. Degree education developed later.

faqs.question: What practical land is described?
faqs.answer: The official about page describes 51.97 hectares, or 128.4 acres, and a crop cafeteria for observing varieties.

faqs.question: Are the website’s admission fees current?
faqs.answer: The admission page includes older guidance and a 2025–26 form. No application charge is presented here as a verified 2026 fee.

faqs.question: Does TRIARD publish placement evidence?
faqs.answer: It publishes named 2025–26 destinations and vacancy notices, but not a verified agriculture placement rate or salary distribution in the material read.

faqs.question: What entry qualification is published for TRIARD?
faqs.answer: Historical official admission page: 10+2 with the listed science combinations, including Physics, Chemistry and Biology or Botany/Zoology. Current subject equivalence and minimum marks must be checked in the entry-year TNAU prospectus.

faqs.answer: https://roeveragri.ac.in/admission/. Read the programme, campus and applicable intake instructions on this official channel.
